podcast.title: Confusion with Warsaw Pact
podcast.body: The band changed their name from "Warsaw" to Joy Division because they were frequently confused with a London metal band named Warsaw Pact, opting to avoid conflict by adopting a new identity. "Warsaw was always getting confused with a London metal band called Warsaw Pact. And rather than get into some kind of fight, they just thought they would change their name."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's the Big Deal About Joy Division?

podcast.title: Demo Tape Recording
podcast.body: On July 18, 1977, Warsaw recorded a demo tape which featured a studio version of the song "At a Later Date." This tape, initially misplaced, provided an early glimpse into their sound. "And that's taken from a long, misplaced demo tape recorded on July 18th, 1977."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's the Big Deal About Joy Division?

podcast.title: Final Gig as Warsaw
podcast.body: The band performed their last gig under the name Warsaw on New Year's Eve, 1977, before officially adopting "Joy Division." "So after one last gig as Warsaw on New Year's Eve 1977, Ian Curtis, Barney Albrecht, soon to become Bernie Sumner, Peter Hook and Steven Morris became Joy Division officially."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's the Big Deal About Joy Division?

podcast.title: First Live Performance
podcast.body: Warsaw performed their first gig on May 29, 1977, at the Electric Circus club in Manchester. The reviews were noted as mixed, yet acknowledged an "elusive spark of dissimilarity" in their sound, hinting at their unique potential. "Warsaw played their first gig on May 29th, 1977, and a Manchester club called the Electric Circus."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's the Big Deal About Joy Division?

podcast.title: Initial Band Name
podcast.body: The band that would become Joy Division initially went by the name "Warsaw" after Ian Curtis rejected "Stiff Kittens." This name was inspired by David Bowie's song "Warzawe" from his "Low" album. "Everyone soon settled on Warsaw. That sounded different."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's the Big Deal About Joy Division?

podcast.title: Precursor to Joy Division
podcast.body: Formed by Bernie and Peter in the spring of 1976, inspired by a Sex Pistols concert in Manchester. This initial group later became Joy Division. "Their first group was called Warsaw. Warsaw became Joy Division."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Search for a Drummer
podcast.body: By 1977, Warsaw was ready to make a demo tape but struggled to find a permanent drummer. Stephen Morris was eventually found in August, as the sole respondent to their advertisement for a drummer in a local music magazine. "By 1977, despite the fact that they couldn't find a permanent drummer, Warsaw was ready to make a demo tape."

xref.title: Formation Inspiration (Spring 1976)
xref.body: Bernie and Peter were motivated to form a band after witnessing a Sex Pistols gig in Manchester. Despite perceiving the performance as "terrible," they found it "great" in its spirit and decided that if the Sex Pistols could perform, they could too. Their initial group was called Warsaw, which subsequently evolved into Joy Division, and later New Order. "If they could do it, maybe we could."

xref.title: Discovery by Rob Gretton (1977)
xref.body: Rob Gretton, a Manchester punk scene figure and DJ, discovered the band formerly known as Warsaw (now trading as Joy Division) performing at approximately two in the morning as part of a talent showcase in 1977. A mere 20-minute set was enough to fully convince Gretton, who then launched a campaign to become their manager and ultimately secured the job.

xref.title: Name Change from Warsaw to Joy Division (1978)
xref.body: When their debut EP was made, the band was still using their original name, Warsaw. However, by the time the record was released in June 1978, they had adopted the name Joy Division. "At the time this record was made, Joy Division was still going by their original name, which was Warsaw, but by the time the record came out, they adopted Joy Division."

xref.body: Warsaw Pact was a London metal band that frequently caused confusion with Joy Division's earlier name, "Warsaw," leading to the latter changing their name to avoid conflict. "Warsaw was always getting confused with a London metal band called Warsaw Pact."

xref.title: Finding a Permanent Drummer
xref.body: The band struggled to find a permanent drummer until August 1977, when Stephen Morris was found. He was the only individual to reply to Warsaw's advertisement for a drummer in a local music magazine, proving to be a good fit. "The next big date in Jordy Vision history was in August, when they finally found a permanent drummer. His name was Stephen Morris."

xref.title: Van Theft & Polish Mafia (Poland)
xref.body: While on tour in Poland one Christmas, NoMeansNo had their rented van stolen after a show in Warsaw, containing about $10,000 worth of merchandise. With local police being unhelpful and the Dutch rental company concerned about insurance coverage outside Holland, a fan connected them with the Polish Mafia. Band member Rob Wright met two heavily armed men in a church basement and negotiated the van's return for 2000 German marks. The next day, the van and all its contents were recovered from a barn outside Warsaw. However, the Warsaw police later demanded another 2000 German marks for operating outside legal channels. "The next day the van was given the name of a village about 100 kilometers outside of Warsaw and told to wait in the town square."
